--- # goimports-reviser ![logo](./images/reviser-muscot_200.png) Tool for Golang to sort goimports by 3-4 groups: std, general, company (optional), and project dependencies. Also formats your code (no need to use `gofmt` or `goimports` separately). ## Features - Sort imports into logical groups (stdlib, general, company, project) - Remove unused imports with `-rm-unused` - Set aliases for versioned packages with `-set-alias` - Format code automatically with `-format` - Apply to directories recursively - Group company imports separately with `-company-prefixes` ## Usage ### Basic command: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ``` ### Apply to a directory recursively: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format -recursive reviser ``` ### Apply to all files: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./... ``` ### Apply to multiple targets: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ./pkg/... ``` ### Options: ```text Usage of goimports-reviser: -apply-to-generated-files Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter. -company-prefixes string Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line. -format Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter. -imports-order string Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. std - std import group; general - libs for general purpose; company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); project - your local project dependencies; blanked - imports with "_" alias; dotted - imports with "." alias. Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project") -list-diff Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter. -local string Deprecated -output string Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file") -project-name string Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter. -recursive Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter. -rm-unused Remove unused imports. Optional parameter. -separate-named Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter. -set-alias Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter. -set-exit-status set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter. -use-cache Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter. -version Show version. ``` ## Examples ### Before usage: ```go package testdata import ( "log" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" "bytes" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" ) ``` ### After usage: ```go package testdata import ( "bytes" "log" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" ) ``` Comments for imports are preserved: ```go package testdata import ( "fmt" // comments to the package here ) ``` ### Example with `-company-prefixes` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimport 3235 characters elided ted file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. --- # goimports-reviser ![logo](./images/reviser-muscot_200.png) Tool for Golang to sort goimports by 3-4 groups: std, general, company (optional), and project dependencies. Also formats your code (no need to use `gofmt` or `goimports` separately). ## Features - Sort imports into logical groups (stdlib, general, company, project) - Remove unused imports with `-rm-unused` - Set aliases for versioned packages with `-set-alias` - Format code automatically with `-format` - Apply to directories recursively - Group company imports separately with `-company-prefixes` ## Usage ### Basic command: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ``` ### Apply to a directory recursively: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format -recursive reviser ``` ### Apply to all files: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./... ``` ### Apply to multiple targets: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ./pkg/... ``` ### Options: ```text Usage of goimports-reviser: -apply-to-generated-files Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter. -company-prefixes string Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line. -format Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter. -imports-order string Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. std - std import group; general - libs for general purpose; company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); project - your local project dependencies; blanked - imports with "_" alias; dotted - imports with "." alias. Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project") -list-diff Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter. -local string Deprecated -output string Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file") -project-name string Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter. -recursive Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter. -rm-unused Remove unused imports. Optional parameter. -separate-named Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter. -set-alias Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter. -set-exit-status set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter. -use-cache Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter. -version Show version. ``` ## Examples ### Before usage: ```go package testdata import ( "log" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" "bytes" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" ) ``` ### After usage: ```go package testdata import ( "bytes" "log" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" ) ``` Comments for imports are preserved: ```go package testdata import ( "fmt" // comments to the package here ) ``` ### Example with `-company-prefixes` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" // fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" // custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` ### Example with `-imports-order std,general,company,project,blanked,dotted` option Before: ```go package testdata // goi 6702 characters elided uld be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. import subprocess, os, shutil
EXE="/workspace/executable"
orig="package p\nimport (\n\"os\"\n\"fmt\"\n)\nvar _,_ = fmt.Println, os.Args\n"
formatted="package p\n\nimport (\n\t\"fmt\"\n\t\"os\"\n)\n\nvar _, _ = fmt.Println, os.Args\n"
def setup(content):
    if os.path.exists("/tmp/projG"): shutil.rmtree("/tmp/projG")
    os.makedirs("/tmp/projG")
    open("/tmp/projG/go.mod",'w').write("module example.com/g\n"); open("/tmp/projG/a.go",'w').write(content)
    old=1000000000; os.utime("/tmp/projG/a.go",(old,old))
for cname,content in [("CHANGED",orig),("UNCHANGED",formatted)]:
 for ld in [False,True]:
  for out in ["file","write","stdout","invalid"]:
    setup(content)
    args=[]
    if ld: args+=["-list-diff"]
    args+=["-output",out,"/tmp/projG/a.go"]
    r=subprocess.run([EXE]+args,capture_output=True,text=True,cwd="/workspace")
    mt=os.stat("/tmp/projG/a.go").st_mtime
    nowritten = (mt==1000000000)
    diskcontent=open("/tmp/projG/a.go").read()
    print(f"{cname:9} ld={ld!s:5} out={out:7} exit={r.returncode} stdout={r.stdout!r} writtenDisk={not nowritten} diskIsFormatted={diskcontent==formatted}")
PY

--- # goimports-reviser ![logo](./images/reviser-muscot_200.png) Tool for Golang to sort goimports by 3-4 groups: std, general, company (optional), and project dependencies. Also formats your code (no need to use `gofmt` or `goimports` separately). ## Features - Sort imports into logical groups (stdlib, general, company, project) - Remove unused imports with `-rm-unused` - Set aliases for versioned packages with `-set-alias` - Format code automatically with `-format` - Apply to directories recursively - Group company imports separately with `-company-prefixes` ## Usage ### Basic command: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ``` ### Apply to a directory recursively: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format -recursive reviser ``` ### Apply to all files: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./... ``` ### Apply to multiple targets: ```bash goimports-reviser -rm-unused -set-alias -format ./reviser/reviser.go ./pkg/... ``` ### Options: ```text Usage of goimports-reviser: -apply-to-generated-files Apply imports sorting and formatting(if the option is set) to generated files. Generated file is a file with first comment which starts with comment '// Code generated'. Optional parameter. -company-prefixes string Company package prefixes which will be placed after 3rd-party group by default(if defined). Values should be comma-separated. Optional parameters. -excludes string Exclude files or dirs, example: '.git/,proto/*.go'. -file-path string Deprecated. Put file name as an argument(last item) of command line. -format Option will perform additional formatting. Optional parameter. -imports-order string Your imports groups can be sorted in your way. std - std import group; general - libs for general purpose; company - inter-org or your company libs(if you set '-company-prefixes'-option, then 4th group will be split separately. In other case, it will be the part of general purpose libs); project - your local project dependencies; blanked - imports with "_" alias; dotted - imports with "." alias. Optional parameter. (default "std,general,company,project") -list-diff Option will list files whose formatting differs from goimports-reviser. Optional parameter. -local string Deprecated -output string Can be "file", "write" or "stdout". Whether to write the formatted content back to the file or to stdout. When "write" together with "-list-diff" will list the file name and write back to the file. Optional parameter. (default "file") -project-name string Your project name(ex.: github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser). Optional parameter. -recursive Apply rules recursively if target is a directory. In case of ./... execution will be recursively applied by default. Optional parameter. -rm-unused Remove unused imports. Optional parameter. -separate-named Separate named imports from their group with a new line. Optional parameter. -set-alias Set alias for versioned package names, like 'github.com/go-pg/pg/v9'. In this case import will be set as 'pg "github.com/go-pg/pg/v9"'. Optional parameter. -set-exit-status set the exit status to 1 if a change is needed/made. Optional parameter. -use-cache Use cache to improve performance. Optional parameter. -version Show version. ``` ## Examples ### Before usage: ```go package testdata import ( "log" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" "bytes" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" ) ``` ### After usage: ```go package testdata import ( "bytes" "log" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/testdata/innderpkg" ) ``` Comments for imports are preserved: ```go package testdata import ( "fmt" // comments to the package here ) ``` ### Example with `-company-prefixes` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" // fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" // custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` ### Example with `-imports-order std,general,company,project,blanked,dotted` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( _ "github.com/pkg1" . "github.com/pkg2" "fmt" //fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" //custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" // fmt package "golang.org/x/exp/slices" // custom package "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" // this is a company package which is not a part of the project, but is a part of your organization "goimports-reviser/pkg" _ "github.com/pkg1" . "github.com/pkg2" ) ``` ### Example with `-format` option Before: ```go package main func test(){ } func additionalTest(){ } ``` After: ```go package main func test(){ } func additionalTest(){ } ``` ### Example with `-separate-named` option Before: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices" ) ``` After: ```go package testdata // goimports-reviser/testdata import ( "fmt" "github.com/incu6us/goimports-reviser/pkg" "golang.org/x/exp/slices" extpkg "google.com/golang/pkg" extslice "github.com/PeterRK/slices" ) ```
